sections.heading: Turn enterprise AI strategy into a practical roadmap
sections.body:
Which AI use cases deserve investment, and what must be in place before they go live? We help business, technology and risk teams agree priorities, ownership and a governed route to delivery.

Competing pilots, unclear value and unclear accountability are reasons to pause and set direction. Agree who owns each use case, what the system may do and where people must oversee it.

[Explore Data & AI](/services/data-ai).

sections.heading: Business value, with clear boundaries
sections.description: Shape an advisory engagement around the decisions you need to make. Agree the depth and format of these outputs during scoping.

sections.heading: From opportunity to accountable delivery
sections.description: Bring the decision-makers together before choosing a model or platform. Each step ends with an output to review and an owner to agree.

items.title: Understand the opportunity — decision brief
items.description: Clarify the business decision, current pilots, constraints and intended users. Agree what value means and which stakeholders must review the scope.

items.title: Prioritise the roadmap — sequenced use cases
items.description: Compare value assumptions, feasibility, dependencies and risk. Agree acceptance criteria and the conditions under which an opportunity should stop, proceed or change.

items.title: Set the guardrails — control responsibilities
items.description: Agree access boundaries, human oversight, approval gates and escalation. Specify cost, quality and tracing requirements for the delivery teams to implement.

items.title: Review and adapt — delivery hand-off
items.description: Route approved work to Agentic AI, Data platforms or Machine learning teams. Review delivery evidence and operating feedback before expanding the roadmap; assign responsibility for reassessing controls.

sections.heading: Choose the right delivery route
sections.description: Agree the operating model here; implement controls with the relevant delivery teams. Advisory, security validation and software are distinct buying decisions.

items.title: From roadmap to implementation
items.description: Move an approved use case into the service that fits the decision and data needs.

items.title: AI security & GRC services
items.description: Scope specialist AI testing, security controls and risk work separately from the governance operating model.

items.title: Linkfields software: AI gateway & guardrails
items.description: AI Governance brings guardrails, cost and tracing through a Linkfields layer built on Portkey and Opik. It does not replace organisational accountability.

sections.note: Products are available by licence, subscription or SaaS, with or without services. Confirm fit and scope; software is not automatically included in an advisory engagement.

sections.heading: An AI decision made accountable
sections.description: Consider an organisation comparing internal knowledge-assistant pilots: leaders need to assess data access, user groups and oversight before deciding where to invest. This illustrative pattern is not a client case or achieved result.

items.title: Make the investment decision
items.description: Compare the pilots against a shared decision brief. Record the value assumptions, readiness gaps and reason to prioritise, defer or stop each one.

items.title: Document ownership and controls
items.description: Agree a roadmap and risk/control record. Name business approval, data access, human-review and escalation owners; identify security validation that needs a specialist team.

items.title: Hand over with acceptance gates
items.description: Give the relevant engineering team the approved scope and control requirements. Agree what evidence will support release and how operational feedback will inform the next investment review.

sections.note: Bring your business priorities, current pilots and governance questions. Together, we can identify stakeholders, agree the initial scope and discuss an appropriate engagement model.

sections.heading: Agree the scope before you commit
sections.description: Start with the decision, current initiatives and main constraint. Select a commercial model around the uncertainty, deliverables and ownership involved.

items.title: Do we need a strategy if pilots already exist?
items.description: A strategy discussion can compare existing pilots, surface dependencies and clarify which deserve further investment. It need not restart useful work; it should make the next decision and its acceptance criteria explicit.

items.title: How does advisory differ from AI Governance software?
items.description: Advisory defines priorities, roles and operating controls. AI Governance software provides a gateway for guardrails, cost and tracing. Security testing and control implementation require their own agreed scope; neither software nor a compliance outcome is an automatic inclusion.

items.title: Which engagement model fits this work?
items.description: Time & Materials suits discovery and evolving roadmaps. Fixed Price suits defined outputs with agreed milestones and acceptance criteria. Dedicated Team, Managed Service or Outcome-Based arrangements can be discussed where responsibilities and measurable outcomes can be agreed and evidenced. [Compare commercial models](/company/our-approach#engagement-models).

items.title: What should we share in the first discussion?
items.description: Describe the business decision, current AI initiatives and main constraint, without sending sensitive documents through the enquiry form. Agree stakeholders and scoping next steps with the team. An NDA can be arranged where required.
